headline_marked: Parliament passes bill to [[dissolve RAB and form SRB]]
headline: Parliament passes bill to dissolve RAB and form SRB
summary: The Special Response Battalion (SRB) will replace the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) as a specialized unit under the police force.
details: The National Parliament has passed the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' through a voice vote on Thursday, effectively dissolving the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).
The new unit, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), will operate under the police force to ensure public security, combat terrorism, and suppress organized crime.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the bill in the third session of the 13th National Parliament, following a review by a parliamentary committee.
Opposition members raised seven objections, arguing that the transition should ensure stronger accountability and national consultation before the formation of the new force.
The opposition's concerns included the speed of the bill's passage, the direct transfer of RAB's manpower and resources to the SRB, and the framework for investigating complaints.
The SRB will be headquartered in Dhaka and will be led by a Director General of at least Additional Inspector General of Police rank.
The government will staff the SRB by appointing or deputing officers and armed personnel from the police and other disciplinary forces as needed.
caption:
RAB is being dissolved. A new specialized police unit, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), will take its place.

The National Parliament has passed the 'Special Response Battalion (SRB) Act, 2026' through a voice vote on Thursday, effectively dissolving the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB).

The new unit, the Special Response Battalion (SRB), will operate under the police force to ensure public security, combat terrorism, and suppress organized crime.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed introduced the bill in the third session of the 13th National Parliament, following a review by a parliamentary committee.

Opposition members raised seven objections, arguing that the transition should ensure stronger accountability and national consultation before the formation of the new force.

The opposition's concerns included the speed of the bill's passage, the direct transfer of RAB's manpower and resources to the SRB, and the framework for investigating complaints.

The SRB will be headquartered in Dhaka and will be led by a Director General of at least Additional Inspector General of Police rank.

The government will staff the SRB by appointing or deputing officers and armed personnel from the police and other disciplinary forces as needed.

headline_marked: Tk 666 crore: [[Grameen Kalyan must pay tax]], HC orders
headline: Tk 666 crore: Grameen Kalyan must pay tax, HC orders
summary: The High Court has dismissed a writ petition by Grameen Kalyan, upholding the National Board of Revenue's tax claim of 666 crore BDT.
details: The High Court has ordered Grameen Kalyan, an organization owned by former interim government chief advisor Muhammad Yunus, to pay 666 crore BDT in taxes to the National Board of Revenue (NBR).
The ruling was delivered on Thursday by a bench led by Justice Mohammad Mojibur Rahman Mia.
Grameen Kalyan had filed a writ petition in 2017 to challenge the legality of the NBR's tax claim.
After an initial hearing, the court had issued a rule, but the new bench has now dismissed the rule and upheld the tax demand.
The organization's lawyer, Abdullah Al Mamun, had previously clarified on July 14 that reports of tax waivers or the withdrawal of the case were 'baseless and misleading'.
caption:
A 666 crore BDT tax bill. The High Court has ruled that Grameen Kalyan must pay up.

The High Court has ordered Grameen Kalyan, an organization owned by former interim government chief advisor Muhammad Yunus, to pay 666 crore BDT in taxes to the National Board of Revenue (NBR).

The ruling was delivered on Thursday by a bench led by Justice Mohammad Mojibur Rahman Mia.

Grameen Kalyan had filed a writ petition in 2017 to challenge the legality of the NBR's tax claim.

After an initial hearing, the court had issued a rule, but the new bench has now dismissed the rule and upheld the tax demand.

The organization's lawyer, Abdullah Al Mamun, had previously clarified on July 14 that reports of tax waivers or the withdrawal of the case were 'baseless and misleading'.
